label: Scaled dot-product attention: queries and keys form a score matrix Q times K-transpose, divided by the square root of d, softmaxed into attention weights, then multiplied by the values V to give the output context vectors.
summary: Q and K produce the scores. V joins at the weighted sum, after softmax.

label: Live computational graph: inputs w, x, b feed z = w x + b, then a = sigmoid(z), then the loss L. Forward values flow right; the gradient of L with respect to each quantity flows back to the left.
summary: Forward values flow down these steps. During backprop, the loss gradients travel back up; the live values below update with the sliders.

label: The chain rule along the path w to z to a to L: the gradient dL/dw is the product of the local derivatives dz/dw = x, da/dz = a(1-a), and dL/da = 2(a-y).
summary: Multiply the local derivatives along this path to obtain the weight’s loss gradient.

label: A CNN: an input image goes through repeated convolution, ReLU and pooling blocks (spatial size shrinks, the number of channels grows), then is flattened into fully-connected layers ending in a softmax over classes.

A feature hierarchy for recognizing a bird: an edge-detection layer feeds part detectors beak and eye, which feed an object-part detector bird's head, which votes among the output classes cat, dog, bird and politician — bird wins.
summary: Edge features support beak and eye detectors; those parts support a bird’s-head feature, which helps the final classification.

label: RAG pipeline: the question is embedded, used to search a vector database of embedded documents, the top-k chunks are retrieved and placed in the prompt alongside the question, and the LLM generates a grounded answer.

Hinton family-tree network: a symbol for person 1 and a symbol for the relationship each map to a learned feature vector; a hidden layer of neurons predicts the output features from the input features; those become the learned features of person 2, which produce the output symbol for person 2.
summary: The person and relationship are parallel inputs. Their learned features combine to predict the related person.

label: Four families of generative model. Autoregressive models factorise the joint probability into a product of conditionals and maximise exact likelihood. Variational autoencoders encode to a latent distribution and maximise a lower bound on the likelihood. Generative adversarial networks train a generator against a discriminator with no likelihood at all. Diffusion models add noise over many steps and learn to reverse it, maximising a bound on the likelihood.
AI Lab banner: the journey from a single neuron, through layers and attention, to a small GPT.
The learning loop used on every page: predict, then play with the interactive demo, then check yourself with the quiz, then rebuild the idea from memory.
summary: Repeat the loop: use what you learned to make your next prediction.

label: Career timeline: 1987 first code on IBM mainframes in Assembler; 1993 to 1994 a PhD-level course on the mathematics of neural networks; 1999 a PhD in Aeronautics and computational engineering; 1999 to 2006 leading university IT services while teaching; 2016 founding an information-security consultancy and audit practice; 2025 using agentic AI professionally.
A multilayer perceptron: two input nodes fully connected to a hidden layer of neurons, which connect to one output neuron.
summary: Each input connects to the hidden neurons. Their activations feed the output neuron.

label: The training loop: forward pass to predict, compute the loss, backward pass for gradients, optimizer step to update weights, then repeat.
summary: Repeat the four steps for each training update.

label: A half adder built from neurons: an AND neuron makes the Carry, a second neuron makes the Sum (XOR).
summary: Both branches receive A and B. Carry and Sum are separate outputs, not consecutive operations.

label: The post-training pipeline: pretraining on web text gives a base LM that knows language; supervised fine-tuning on instruction demonstrations makes it follow instructions; preference tuning with RLHF or DPO on human rankings makes it helpful, harmless and honest.

LoRA: keep the big pretrained weight matrix W frozen, and learn a small low-rank update B times A (with rank r much smaller than the dimension), so the effective weight is W plus B A. Only the tiny B and A are trained.

An RNN drawn two ways: folded as one cell whose hidden state feeds back into itself (recurrent weight Wh), with input weight Wx and output weight Wy; and unrolled over time as a chain h0 to h3 where each step takes an input x_t, updates the state, and emits y_t.
summary: Each time step receives its own x and produces its own y. The hidden state passes to the next step; all steps reuse the same weights.

label: The chain from a single neuron to a GPT: one neuron → logic gate → a layer → MLP → Transformer → LLM, each step a weighted sum plus a nonlinearity.
A single neuron: three inputs are each multiplied by a weight, summed with a bias, then passed through an activation to produce one output number.
Scale: one neuron, then a layer of a few, then a GPT — the same unit repeated up to about a hundred billion times.
The same neuron seen two ways: a logic view (neuron → gate → circuit → computer) and a function view (neuron → MLP → any function); a trained network is both at once.
summary: These are two views of the same neuron, not competing stages in a single pipeline.

label: The two paradigms of intelligence (Geoffrey Hinton). The logic-inspired approach: intelligence is reasoning via symbolic rules, and learning can wait. The biologically-inspired approach: intelligence is learning the connection strengths in a neural network, and reasoning can wait. This lab follows the biologically-inspired approach.

A Transformer block: input embeddings, then LayerNorm and causal self-attention with a residual add, then LayerNorm and a feed-forward MLP with a residual add; stacked N times, then a linear layer and softmax over the vocabulary giving next-token probabilities.
summary: Within each repeated block, a skip connection adds the attention input after attention; another adds the MLP input after the MLP.

label: Two-neuron network: inputs x0 and x1 feed a hidden neuron h and also skip directly to the output neuron y; y combines x0, x1 and h to compute XOR.
summary: The output receives both original inputs directly as skip connections, as well as the hidden neuron’s output.

label: Schematic of one neuron: each input times its weight is summed with a bias to give z, then an activation phi gives the output a.
Two panels. Left: a larger weight makes the sigmoid switch steeper. Right: the bias slides the same switch left or right.

A guide to choosing an activation. Ask which layer: hidden layers use ReLU by default, GELU or SiLU for transformers, Leaky ReLU or ELU for dead units, and avoid sigmoid or tanh deep. Output layers pick by task: linear for regression, sigmoid for binary, softmax for multiclass, sigmoid per class for multi-label — each paired with its matching loss.

Left: a central blue cluster surrounded by a red ring cannot be split by any single straight line, which is all a stack of linear layers can produce. Right: a nonlinear network bends the boundary into a closed curve that cleanly encloses the blue cluster.
AND is separable by one straight line; XOR is not — its two 1-corners sit on opposite diagonals.
Anatomy of a biological neuron
summary: Follow the signal from dendrites and soma, along the axon, to its terminals.

label: A synapse transmitting a signal
summary: Vesicles release neurotransmitters into the cleft; they bind receptors on the receiving neuron.

label: Mapping between biological and artificial neuron parts
Threshold Logic Unit: inputs times weights, summed, then thresholded to a 0/1 output
summary: The threshold logic unit returns 0 or 1 according to whether the weighted sum reaches its threshold.

label: A matrix is a linear transformation: the unit square with basis vectors e1 and e2 on the left becomes a sheared, scaled parallelogram on the right, whose edges are the columns of W — the images of e1 and e2.
summary: The edges after transformation are the columns of W: the images of the two basis vectors.

label: Four distribution shapes side by side: a symmetric bell (normal), a flat box (uniform), a decaying curve (exponential), and a right-skewed hump with a long right tail.

Gradient descent on the same quadratic bowl with three learning rates. Too small: tiny steps that crawl. Just right: a few steps converge to the bottom. Too big: steps overshoot and bounce across the valley without settling.

Left: a convex loss is a single bowl, so descent always reaches the global minimum. Right: a non-convex loss has several dips, and gradient descent can get stuck in a local minimum that is not the global one.

Naive softmax on large logits 1000, 1001, 1002 overflows: exp gives infinity and infinity over infinity is NaN. Subtracting the max first gives logits -2, -1, 0, exp gives finite values, and softmax returns a valid probability distribution.
The 32 bits of a float32: 1 sign bit, 8 exponent bits, and 23 mantissa (fraction) bits. Its value is minus-one to the sign, times 1 point mantissa, times two to the (exponent minus 127).
Three panels on the same data. Left: a straight line underfits. Middle: a smooth curve fits well. Right: a wiggly high-degree curve overfits by chasing the noise.
Left: a decision tree of threshold questions with three leaves A, B, C. Right: the same rules chop the 2D feature space into three axis-aligned rectangles labeled A, B, C.

sections.title: The same regions in feature space

label: Two panels. Small C gives a wide street that tolerates a few points violating the margin. Large C gives a narrow street that hugs the points to avoid violations.

Left: in one dimension the blue class is in the middle and red on both ends, so no single threshold separates them. Right: adding an x-squared coordinate lifts the points onto a parabola, where one straight horizontal line cleanly separates blue (low) from red (high).
summary: Adding x² makes it possible to separate the classes with one straight line in the lifted feature space.

label: Two interleaving crescent clusters. Left: k-means with k=2 splits them with a straight cut and mixes the crescents. Right: DBSCAN follows the density and recovers the two crescents correctly.
5-fold cross-validation: the data is split into 5 equal parts; across 5 rounds each part is used once as the validation set while the other four train the model, and the scores are averaged.
summary: Split the data into five parts. In each round, the named fold is validation data and the other four folds are training data.

label: Grid search vs random search with 9 trials each. The grid's 9 points fall on only 3 distinct values of the important (horizontal) parameter; random search's 9 points give 9 distinct values, covering the important axis much better.

Nested cross-validation: an outer 3-fold loop where each round holds out a test fold, and inside each outer training part an inner 3-fold loop rotates a validation fold to choose hyperparameters. The outer test folds, never seen by tuning, give the honest score.
summary: For each outer round, tune inside the outer training data. Evaluate the chosen setting on that round’s untouched outer test fold.

sections.title: Resplit only the outer training data

label: Left, a learning curve: training error stays near zero while validation error falls as data grows but keeps a gap — the signature of high variance. Right, a validation curve: training error keeps dropping with tree depth while validation error bottoms out near depth 5 then flattens — the sweet spot.

The end-to-end machine learning workflow: Data, Clean and split, Features, Train, Validate and tune, Deploy and monitor, connected left to right, with a dashed feedback loop from monitoring back to features.
summary: Monitoring provides new data and can trigger retraining, closing the loop.

label: Before scaling, income's raw range 0 to 100000 fills the axis while age 0 to 80 is a tiny sliver on the same scale, so distance-based models ignore age. After standardizing, income and age span the same range and both count.
One-hot encoding turns a single 'color' column with values red, green, blue, red into three 0/1 columns is_red, is_green, is_blue, where exactly one column is 1 per row.
summary: The output tuple is ordered (is_red, is_green, is_blue). Each row activates exactly its own category.

label: A class distribution of 950 negatives to 50 positives (95 to 5 percent). A model always predicting negative scores 95 percent accuracy yet catches zero positives. After rebalancing — oversampling/SMOTE, undersampling, or class weights — the two classes are even.
A neuron's straight decision line splits the plane into a 1 side and a 0 side; the weight vector points to the 1 side at right angles, and distance from the line is confidence.
The weight vector and the input vector with the angle theta between them; output is largest when they align.
Shapes of the step, sigmoid, tanh and ReLU activation functions on shared axes
Gradient size versus network depth: ReLU stays at 1 while the sigmoid product vanishes toward zero.
Two vectors a and b drawn from the origin with the angle theta between them. The projection of b onto a is b's shadow along a, found by dropping a perpendicular from the tip of b to the line of a.
An eigenvector v lies on a dashed line; applying W only stretches it to lambda v along the same line, while a non-eigenvector u is rotated to a new direction Wu.
A cloud of data points forms an elongated blob; PCA finds the principal axes — a long arrow PC1 along the direction of most variance and a short perpendicular arrow PC2.
A curve f(x) with the tangent line at a point P; the tangent's slope, rise over run, is the derivative f-prime at P.

Concentric circular contours of a bowl with its minimum at the centre. At a point P the gradient points radially outward (steepest ascent), the negative gradient points inward toward the minimum (steepest descent), and both are perpendicular to the contour through P.
The normal bell curve centred at the mean. About 68 percent of the area lies within one standard deviation, 95 percent within two, and 99.7 percent within three.

Minimizing x squared plus y squared subject to x plus y equals 1: concentric level circles centered at the origin are tangent to the constraint line at (0.5, 0.5), where the gradient of f is parallel to the gradient of g.
Binary entropy as a function of the coin bias p: a dome peaking at 1 bit when p is 0.5 (maximum uncertainty) and dropping to 0 at p=0 and p=1 (a certain outcome).

Cross-entropy as a function of the predicted probability q when the true bias is 0.7. The curve is a valley reaching its minimum exactly at q equals 0.7, and rising steeply as q approaches 0 (confident and wrong).
Scatter of eight data points with the best-fit straight line; each pink vertical segment is a residual, the gap between a point and the line.
The mean squared error drawn as a convex bowl over the weight w; gradient descent takes steps downhill, large when far away and small near the bottom, converging at the minimum.
As model capacity grows, training error keeps falling while test error follows a U-shape, reaching a minimum at the sweet spot before rising due to overfitting.
The logistic sigmoid squashes any real score z into a probability between 0 and 1, crossing 0.5 at z=0 and saturating toward 0 and 1 in the tails.
Two classes of points in 2D separated by a single straight decision boundary; one side is predicted class 1, the other class 0.
A regression tree predicts a piecewise-constant staircase. A shallow depth-2 tree makes a few wide steps; a deep depth-6 tree makes many narrow steps that chase the noisy data points.
Gradient boosting starts from the flat mean F0 and adds shallow trees one at a time; after 1 tree the fit is coarse, after 8 closer, after 60 it tracks the data well.
Several thin lines can separate the two classes, but the SVM chooses the boundary sitting in the middle of the widest empty street; the two points touching the street edges are the support vectors.
A support vector machine separates two classes with the widest possible street: a solid boundary line, two dashed margin lines, and the circled points touching them are the support vectors.

Three classification losses versus the margin: the 0/1 loss is a step at zero, the hinge loss falls linearly and becomes exactly zero once the margin passes 1 (with a kink there), and the log loss is smooth and never reaches zero.
k-means clustering with k equals 3: points colored by their assigned cluster, with an X marking each cluster's centroid (mean).
Elbow plot: k-means inertia drops steeply from k=1 to k=3 then flattens, so the elbow at k=3 is the suggested number of clusters.
A dendrogram of six points A to F merged bottom-up at increasing distances; a dashed horizontal cut line crosses three branches, giving three clusters: A-B-C, D-E, and F.

A tilted 2-D point cloud with its principal components drawn as axes through the centroid: PC1 is the long axis along the direction of greatest spread (95% of the variance), PC2 the short perpendicular axis (5%).
